drafts.title: Lightweight In-Browser LLMs for JSON to Chart.js Config Conversion?
drafts.body:
I'm looking into running small language models entirely in the browser to convert JSON data into valid Chart.js configurations. The goal is to keep everything lightweight and client-side, but the hardware and browser environments of users are unknown, which complicates tool selection.

Has anyone found effective in-browser inference frameworks that handle this kind of structured generation well without heavy dependencies? Given the variability in users' setups, I'm curious about practical tradeoffs or recommendations for frameworks that balance model size, speed, and reliability in-browser.

Any experiences or pointers to lightweight tools that can specifically assist with JSON-to-Chart.js config generation would be really helpful.

drafts.title: Best Lightweight Browser-Based LLM Tools for Chart.js Config Generation from JSON?
drafts.body:
Exploring small LLM inference fully in-browser for generating Chart.js configs from JSON objects raises questions about suitable lightweight frameworks. Since user hardware and browsers are unknown, the challenge is finding tools that run efficiently without server dependencies.

Are there any in-browser LLM inference solutions known to handle JSON-to-Chart.js config tasks well, while maintaining low resource use? Understanding the tradeoffs between model size, inference speed, and accuracy in this context would help.

If anyone has insights or has tested frameworks focused on this use case, sharing those would clarify what’s feasible given the constraints.
